classes.finest_note: Ballots from every polling place in a counting district are mixed before counting (公職選挙法 art. 66), so no polling-place results exist; the counting district (municipality, ward, or a numbered piece of a split one) is the finest unit.
classes.note: Counted per constituency: 1947-1993 SNTV in multi-member districts; from 1996 the single-member districts plus the 11 PR blocks (300 + 11 to 2012, 295 + 11 in 2014, 289 + 11 since 2017). Pre-1996 district counts and seats are read from the 選挙制度 box of each Wikipedia election article (第23回 to 第40回; the 1人区 Amami district counts from 1955); the MIC 結果調 books were not reachable.

cadence.vacancy_rule: Vacancies are filled from the PR list or by by-elections held on the fourth Sundays of April and October (公職選挙法 art. 33-2).

classes.name: 日本国憲法の改正の国民投票
classes.note: Provided by Constitution art. 96 and the 2007 procedure act (in force 2010); never held.
classes.disposition_reason: Never held: no amendment has been initiated by the Diet since the 2007 procedure act.

classes.name: 内閣総理大臣の指名
classes.disposition_reason: The Diet designates the Prime Minister by a vote of its members (Constitution art. 67); party presidential elections are internal. Neither is a public election.

classes.name: 海区漁業調整委員会委員選挙
classes.disposition_reason: The electorate is licensed fishers under the Fisheries Act, an occupational vote; most seats are uncontested.

classes.name: 帝国議会衆議院議員総選挙
classes.name_en: Imperial Diet House of Representatives elections
classes.note: Twenty-two general elections from 1 July 1890 to 10 April 1946 under the Meiji Constitution (restricted male suffrage, manhood suffrage from 1928, women from 1946). The House secretariat's 衆議院議員総選挙一覧 covers the 1st to 31st elections by district and is in NDL Digital Collections.

classes.name: 都道府県知事選挙
classes.note: Plurality with a quarter of valid votes required (法定得票, else a rerun). Four-year terms on staggered cycles: each election falls when the incumbent's term ends or on resignation, so only some prefectures vote in the unified local elections. Year entries 2009-2026 count the governors whose terms expire that year (MIC 任期満了に関する調); earlier years expect the official count over the term; early vacancies add elections.

classes.name: 都道府県議会議員選挙
classes.note: SNTV and plurality in districts of cities, counties, and wards. 41 assemblies vote in the unified local elections each April of years 3 mod 4; Tokyo, Ibaraki, Iwate, Miyagi, Fukushima, and Okinawa vote on their own cycles after early dissolutions. Year entries 2009-2026 count the assemblies whose terms expire that year (MIC 任期満了に関する調); earlier years expect the official count over the term.
classes.disposition_reason: No national canvass with candidate votes exists. The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications' 地方選挙結果調 books (2003-2019) hold prefectural assembly statistics only as counts by prefecture (candidates, winners, turnout, party and age tallies) for the April unified elections, not votes by candidate and district; those sit with each of the 47 prefectural election commissions, one site and format apiece.

classes.name: 市区町村長選挙
classes.name_en: Mayors of cities, towns, villages, and Tokyo special wards
classes.note: About 1,741 offices (1,718 municipalities and the 23 special wards), plurality with the quarter threshold; staggered four-year cycles, about a quarter in the unified local elections. The 20 designated-city mayors are inside this class.

classes.name: 市区町村議会議員選挙
classes.note: At-large SNTV (designated cities by ward) with a quarter-of-quota threshold; staggered four-year cycles.
classes.disposition_reason: No national canvass exists. The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications publishes only national totals by party for the unified local elections, plus candidate results for designated-city mayors; candidate votes for the roughly 1,740 city, town, village, and special-ward assemblies sit with each municipal election commission, one site and format apiece.

classes.name: 住民投票
classes.name_en: Local referendums (ordinance, merger, and special-ward votes)
classes.note: Advisory votes under each municipality's or prefecture's own ordinance (Maki nuclear plant 1996, Okinawa prefecture 1996 and 2019, hundreds of merger votes in 2001-2006), and the binding Osaka special-ward votes under the 2012 act (2015-05-17 and 2020-11-01). Prefectural ones are included here.

cadence.locator: https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/424AC1000000080 (art. 7: 特別区の設置についての投票)

classes.name: 地方自治特別法の住民投票
classes.note: A law applying to one local body needs its residents' consent by vote (Constitution art. 95; 地方自治法 arts. 261-262). Held for about 15 laws in 1949-1952 (Hiroshima and Nagasaki peace cities, international tourism cities, and others); none since. The cities and dates are not yet confirmed from an official list.

classes.name: 解職・解散の投票（リコール）
classes.locator: https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/322AC0000000067 (arts. 76-85: a petition of a third of the electorate forces a vote on dissolving the assembly or removing the head or a member)
classes.note: Called by residents' petitions; mostly in towns and villages, a few in cities and none yet for a governor. Each commission publishes its own.

classes.name: 教育委員会委員選挙
classes.note: Prefectural and municipal boards of education were elected under the 1948 Board of Education Act (elections in 1948, 1950, 1952, and 1954) until the 1956 act made them appointed.

classes.name: 農業委員会委員選挙
classes.note: Farmers elected most members of each municipal agricultural committee every three years under the Agricultural Committee Act until the 2016 reform made them appointed; most seats went uncontested.
classes.disposition_reason: An occupational electorate (registered farmers) under the Agricultural Committee Act, abolished in 2016; most seats were uncontested and results were kept only by each committee.

classes.name: 財産区議会議員選挙
classes.note: A few hundred property wards (財産区) that hold forests or hot springs for a former village elect an assembly under the Public Offices Election Act; most are uncontested.
